channel.title: How Biscuit
channel.description: Practical, evidence-aware guides for technology, home, kitchens, shopping decisions, and useful tools.

item.title: Why Is My Electric Bill So High in Summer?
item.description: A high summer electric bill usually comes from more cooling hours, higher rates, a longer billing period, air leaks, or an inefficient system. Here is how to identify the cause.

item.title: How Much Does a Window AC Cost per Hour?
item.description: Calculate a window air conditioner’s hourly, daily, and monthly electricity cost from its wattage and your local electric rate.

item.title: 2.4 GHz vs. 5 GHz Wi-Fi: Which Should You Use?
item.description: Use 2.4 GHz when range and wall penetration matter; use 5 GHz when a nearby device needs more capacity. Learn why the router may choose automatically.

item.title: Best Place to Put Your Wi-Fi Router
item.description: Put your router near the center of the area you use, out in the open, off the floor, and away from dense barriers. Use this test before buying an extender.

item.title: Fan vs. Air Conditioner Cost: How Much Cheaper Is a Fan?
item.description: A fan usually costs far less to run than an air conditioner, but it does not lower room temperature. Compare hourly costs and learn when to use each.

item.title: How to Fix Wi-Fi Dead Zones Without Buying Anything
item.description: Map the weak area, move and raise the router, try another band, reduce interference, and test one change at a time before buying mesh or an extender.

item.title: Home Wi-Fi Dead-Zone Checklist
item.description: Record Wi-Fi performance room by room, test one change at a time, and decide whether the problem is your device, router placement, or internet service.

item.title: Why Does My Wi-Fi Keep Disconnecting?
item.description: Repeated Wi-Fi drops can come from weak signal, one problem device, modem trouble, power saving, saved settings, or router faults. Diagnose them in this order.

item.title: Why Is My Wi-Fi So Slow? 12 Things to Check Before Buying Anything
item.description: Slow Wi-Fi can come from weak signal, ISP trouble, congestion, router placement, or one problem device. Use this step-by-step diagnosis before buying new hardware.

item.title: How Much Does a Portable AC Cost to Run?
item.description: Calculate a portable air conditioner’s hourly and monthly electricity cost using its watts, runtime, and your local electricity rate.

item.title: Does Turning the AC Off Save Money?
item.description: Turning off or raising the AC when no one is home usually saves energy, but heat, humidity, pets, and health needs determine whether “off” is sensible.

item.title: Home Energy Check for a High Summer Electric Bill
item.description: Use this step-by-step home energy checklist to find why a summer electric bill increased, from billing days and rates to AC filters, air leaks, and hidden loads.

item.title: Why Salt Melts Ice (and When It Stops Working)
item.description: A plain-English field guide to freezing-point depression, brine, the limits of rock salt, and the least-wasteful way to de-ice a walk.

item.title: How Does Baking Powder Work?
item.description: Baking powder makes batter and dough rise by producing carbon dioxide bubbles. Here is what triggers it, what goes wrong, and how to test your can.

item.title: Why Are Some Answers Better Than Others?
item.description: A useful answer addresses the real question, explains its reasoning, shows the next move, and makes the limits of its evidence visible.
